Template-free retrosynthesis models (MEGAN and RootAligned) generalize better to novel reaction disconnections and out-of-distribution templates than the template-based LocalRetro model, as measured by higher top-k accuracy on the narrow split and Pistachio OOD test sets.

If template-free retrosynthesis models are trained under data-split regimes that increase exposure to novel reaction templates or products, then they will achieve higher top-k accuracy than template-based models on out-of-distribution test reactions involving unseen disconnections or products, because they learn generalizable chemical reactivity patterns rather than relying on explicit, frequency-biased reaction templates.

If template-free retrosynthesis models learn implicit chemical transformations while template-based models depend on a fixed set of extracted reaction templates, then template-free models will achieve higher top-10 accuracy on narrow-split and Pistachio OOD evaluations, whereas template-based LocalRetro will achieve higher top-10 accuracy on broad-split and Pistachio ID evaluations, because template coverage and frequency bias limit generalization to unseen disconnections but aid prediction when templates are known.

Single-step retrosynthesis models that do not use explicit reaction templates generalize better to novel reaction disconnections and products than template-based models, as evaluated by top-k and round-trip accuracy on narrow-split, broad-split, and external Pistachio test sets.

If single-step retrosynthesis models are trained and evaluated on splits that independently control product novelty and template disconnection novelty, then template-free models will generalize better to unseen reaction templates and rare disconnections than template-based models because they learn implicit transformation patterns rather than relying on a fixed set of extracted reaction templates.

If single-step retrosynthesis models are evaluated under splitting strategies that control template coverage, then template-free models will achieve higher top-k accuracy than template-based models on reactions requiring novel disconnections (unseen templates), whereas template-based models will maintain higher accuracy on in-distribution disconnections and show greater performance degradation when training template diversity is restricted, because template-free architectures learn generalizable disconnection patterns rather than relying on a fixed, frequency-biased template library.
